Q1.baseline: passable mask/polygons -> skeleton or centerline graph -> edge length + simple deterministic visibility/scene-change descriptors -> k-shortest/beam/RCSP candidate pool -> raw objective registry (interest, length, repeat) -> feasibility-first selection
Q1.author_route: weighted five-index interest + route cost + claimed improved GA with roulette/crossover/mutation; printed appendix instead contains Dijkstra and separate scenic-score scripts
alternatives: epsilon-constraint or resource-constrained shortest path on reduced graph
genuine NSGA-II/GA with path-preserving encoding when exact enumeration is infeasible
not_recommended: arbitrary vector one-point crossover on node sequences without adjacency repair
letting nearest-component straight-line bridges enter the final graph without walkability proof
calling a Dijkstra appendix implementation evidence for GA
Q1.why_select: the geometry and interpretable scene-change representation are reusable; optimizer should be chosen only after graph size and exact-gap feasibility are known
Q1.switch_condition: promote evolutionary search only if bounded/exact candidate methods are too expensive and same-budget independent evaluation shows stable gain while preserving final route feasibility

Q2.baseline: deterministic grid/subregion landscape descriptors + simple KMeans/agglomerative diagnostic + optional spatial smoothing + non-circular scaling + transparent weighted score + full garden-by-run sensitivity matrix
Q2.author_route: GMM-MRF with EM/ICM/BIC + open-close/rhythm features + Jichang reference normalization + perturbation analysis; printed code collapses to KMeans/random openness/hard-coded sensitivity inputs
alternatives: GaussianMixture + BIC without MRF, then add Potts/graph smoothing only if spatial fragmentation remains
spatially constrained agglomerative/Spectral clustering on adjacency graph
pairwise/ordinal preference model if independent expert labels are sufficiently large
not_recommended: using random placeholder features inside real-garden scoring
using the calibration anchor's top rank as validation
computing Kendall tau between parameter-scenario order and garden order
Q2.why_select: small n favors auditable descriptors and transparent calibration; sophisticated spatial probabilistic models need actual likelihood/adjacency primitives and independent evidence
Q2.switch_condition: promote GMM-MRF when enough subregions exist, spatial coherence matters, and BIC/held-out likelihood/spatial stability clearly improves over simple clustering

Q3.baseline: compact heterogeneous garden descriptor -> train/reference-fitted robust scaling by feature block -> cosine/Euclidean/Gower for continuous features + explicit set or weighted-minmax composition similarity -> externally defined pair/preference validation + hierarchical clustering as descriptive output
Q3.author_route: unscaled-appearing composite vector + cosine/set-Jaccard fusion, alpha selected on internal clustering stability, Heyuan external application; printed code only hard-codes post-adjusted Heyuan similarities
alternatives: Gower distance for mixed-scale mixed-type data
PCA/factor reduction after standardization and redundancy audit
metric learning only with many independent gardens and external pairwise labels
not_recommended: raw cosine over length/count and [0,1] features without documented scaling
individual post-hoc sign/offset correction of selected similarities
calling an unlabeled external application accuracy validation
Q3.why_select: with roughly ten reference gardens, compact standardized metrics and transparent similarity semantics dominate high-capacity learned metrics
Q3.switch_condition: use learned metric/multimodal embeddings only when independent garden count and external preference labels support held-out validation; otherwise preserve descriptive similarity status
